source_text: Εἰκότως ἄρα ὁ θεσπέσιος ἀπόστολος κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν φησὶν ἐγνωρίσθη μοι τὸ μυστήριον, καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ, πρὸς ὃ δύνασθε ἀναγινώσκοντες νοῆσαι τὴν σύνεσίν μου ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃ ἑτέραις γενεαῖς οὐκ ἐγνωρίσθη τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὡς νῦν ἀπεκαλύφθη τοῖς ἁγίοις ἀποστόλοις αὐτοῦ καὶ προφήταις. ἔστιν γάρ τις καὶ τελείων μάθησις, περὶ ἧς πρὸς τοὺς Κολοσσαεῖς γράφων φησίν· οὐ παυόμεθα ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι καὶ αἰτούμενοι, ἵνα πληρωθῆτε τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ συνέσει πνευματικῇ, περιπατῆσαι ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου εἰς πᾶσαν ἀρέσκειαν, παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ καρποφοροῦντες καὶ αὐξανόμενοι τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει ἐνδυναμούμενοι κατὰ τὸ κράτος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ. καὶ πάλιν κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι φησὶν εἰς ὑμᾶς πληρῶσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ μυστήριον τὸ ἀποκεκρυμμένον ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν γενεῶν, ὃ νῦν ἐφανερώθη τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ, οἷς ἠθέλησεν ὁ θεὸς γνωρίσαι, τί τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τοῦ μυστηρίου τούτου ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. ὥστε ἄλλα μὲν τὰ μυστήρια τὰ ἀποκεκρυμμένα ἄχρι τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ ὑπ’ αὐτῶν παραδοθέντα ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου παρειλήφασιν (ἀποκεκρυμμένα δὲ ἐν τῇ παλαιᾷ διαθήκῃ), ἃ νῦν ἐφανερώθη τοῖς ἁγίοις, ἄλλο δὲ τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, ὅ ἐστιν ἡ πίστις καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡ εἰς Χριστόν, ὃν ἀλλαχῇ θεμέλιον εἴρηκεν. καὶ πάλιν οἷον φιλοτιμούμενος ἐμφῆναι τὴν γνῶσιν ὧδέ πως γράφει· νουθετοῦντες πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ, ἵνα παραστήσωμεν πάντα ἄνθρωπον τέλειον ἐν Χριστῷ· οὐ πάντα ἁπλῶς ἄνθρωπον, ἐπεὶ οὐδεὶς ἂν ἦν ἄπιστος, οὐδὲ μὴν πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα τέλειον ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλὰ πάντα ἄνθρωπον λέγει, ὡς εἰπεῖν ὅλον τὸν ἄνθρωπον, οἷον σώματι καὶ ψυχῇ ἡγνισμένον, ἐπεί, ὅτι οὐ πάντων ἡ γνῶσις, διαρρήδην ἐπιφέρει· συμβιβασθέντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰς πᾶν πλοῦτος τῆς πληροφορίας τῆς συνέσεως, εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ, ἐν ᾧ εἰσι πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ τῆς γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι. τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτερεῖτε, γρηγοροῦντες ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ· ἡ εὐχαριστία δὲ οὐκ ἐπὶ ψυχῆς μόνον καὶ τῶν πνευματικῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματος γίνεται καὶ τῶν τοῦ σώματος ἀγαθῶν. καὶ ἔτι σαφέστερον ἐκκαλύπτει τὸ μὴ πάντων εἶναι τὴν γνῶσιν, ἐπιλέγων· προσευχόμενοι ἅμα καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὁ θεὸς ἀνοίξῃ ἡμῖν θύραν τοῦ λαλῆσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ ὃ καὶ δέδεμαι, ἵνα φανερώσω αὐτὸ ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι. ἦν γάρ τινα ἀγράφως παραδιδόμενα. αὐτίκα τοῖς Ἑβραίοις καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον φησίν, ὡς ἂν ἐγγηράσαντες τῇ διαθήκῃ τῇ παλαιᾷ, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς, τίνα τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος καὶ οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς·
pass_a_gloss: It is reasonable therefore that the divine apostle says according to revelation, the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote in brief, so that you, reading, may understand my understanding in the mystery of Christ, which was not made known to the sons of men in other generations, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets. For there is also a perfection of knowledge, about which, writing to the Colossians, he says: we do not cease praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, to walk worthily of the Lord to all pleasing, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God, being empowered in all power according to the strength of his glory. And again, according to the plan of God given to me, he says to fill in you the word of God, the mystery hidden from the ages and from the generations, which has now been made manifest to his holy ones, to whom God willed to make known what the wealth of the glory of this mystery is among the nations. So the other mysteries, which were hidden until the apostles and handed down by them as from the Lord, having been hidden in the old covenant, have now been made manifest to the holy ones, but the wealth of the glory of the mystery among the nations is another, which is the faith and hope in Christ, whom he has called the foundation elsewhere. And again, as if eager to show the knowledge, he writes thus: admonishing every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ, not every person simply, since no one would be faithless, nor every believer perfect in Christ, but every person, as if the whole person, purified in body and soul, since not everyone has knowledge, he explicitly states: being united in love and to all wealth of full assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God in Christ, in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden. Be devoted to prayer, watching in it with thanksgiving; thanksgiving is not only for the soul and spiritual goods, but also for the body and the goods of the body. And even more clearly, he reveals that not everyone has knowledge, adding: praying at the same time also for us, that God may open to us a door to speak the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am also bound, so that I may make it clear as I ought to speak. For there were some things handed down unwritten. Immediately, to the Hebrews, and for they ought to be teachers because of time, he says, as if they had become old in the old covenant, you again have need to be taught what the elements of the beginning of the words of God are, and you have become those having need of milk and not solid food;

choices.why: passive voice indicates the subject received the knowledge
refers to a state of completeness or maturity
indicates the mystery is now revealed

bible_refs.note: knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding

pass_b_english: It is entirely reasonable that the divinely inspired apostle declares the mystery was made known to him by revelation, just as he wrote briefly, so that when you read it you may grasp his insight into the mystery of Christ (Ephesians 3:3-4). That mystery was not disclosed to the sons of men in earlier generations, but it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets (Ephesians 3:5). There is indeed a perfection of knowledge, and concerning it he writes to the Colossians: "We have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, so that you may walk worthily of the Lord, fully pleasing to him, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God, being strengthened with all power according to the might of his glory" (Colossians 1:9-10). Again, in line with the stewardship of God entrusted to me for your sake, he says he became a minister to fulfill the word of God — the mystery hidden from the ages and from generations, but now made manifest to his saints, to whom God chose to make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the nations (Colossians 1:25-27).

Thus other mysteries that were concealed until the apostles and then handed down by them as received from the Lord — hidden in the Old Covenant — have now been revealed to the saints; but the riches of the glory of the mystery among the nations is something different: it is the faith and hope that rest on Christ, whom he elsewhere calls the foundation (1 Corinthians 3:11). Once more, as if eager to display this knowledge, he writes: "We admonish everyone with all wisdom, that we may present everyone mature in Christ" (Colossians 1:28). He does not mean every person without distinction, for then no one would be an unbeliever; nor does he mean that every believer is already mature in Christ. Rather, by "every person" he means, so to speak, the whole person — purified in body and soul. Since not everyone possesses this knowledge, he adds explicitly that they are "knit together in love, and to all the riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God, namely Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Colossians 2:2-3).

"Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving" (Colossians 4:2); and thanksgiving is offered not only for the soul and spiritual blessings, but also for the body and the goods of the body. He makes it even clearer that not everyone possesses this knowledge when he adds: "At the same time, pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison — that I may make it clear, as I ought to speak" (Colossians 4:3-4). For there were certain things handed down without writing. At once, to the Hebrews he says: since they ought to be teachers by reason of time, they have become, as it were, aged in the Old Covenant; yet you have need again for someone to teach you the elementary principles of the oracles of God, and you have become those who need milk and not solid food (Hebrews 5:12).

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal translation of the entire span, while Pass B provides a more idiomatic version with appropriate scripture citations (Ephesians 3:3-4, Colossians 1:9-10, Colossians 1:25-27, 1 Corinthians 3:11, Colossians 1:28, Colossians 2:2-3, Colossians 4:2, Colossians 4:3-4, Hebrews 5:12) which match the quoted/alluded content in the Greek. All clauses, including the distinction between the 'whole person' (body and soul) and the 'other mysteries', are preserved.
